official.deadline_note: Application period for Master's programmes taught in English for the September 2027 intake: 7 January to 21 January 2027 (first joint national application round, via Studyinfo). Economics and Business Administration programmes also have an early application period from 1 October to 15 October 2026 for the September 2027 intake. UEF does not publish a separate scholarship deadline: the first-year Early Bird discount is triggered by accepting the admission offer and paying the tuition fee, or its first instalment, within 21 days of the publication of the admission results, with the exact date given in the admission letter; any second instalment and all later annual tuition fees are due by 31 August.
official.status_note: The official page (updated 3 August 2026) publishes the tuition waivers for the 2027 intake: the Early Bird discount for the first academic year and the 30% progress-based waivers for later years. From the date of verification, the remaining published application window is the first joint national application round opening 7 January 2027.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The tuition fee for international Bachelor's and Master's degree programmes is EUR 10,000-12,000 per academic year depending on the programme, and for Master's students the fee remains the same for the whole duration of the degree. The Early Bird discount and tuition waivers available at UEF generally cover up to 30% of the tuition fee.
benefits: Early Bird discount of 30% of the first academic year's tuition fee, i.e. EUR 3,000 for EUR 10,000 programmes and EUR 3,600 for EUR 12,000 programmes

30% tuition waiver for the second and third year of bachelor's studies and the second year of master's studies, awarded on the basis of academic progress (at least 55 ECTS credits completed during the first academic year and included in the approved Personal Study Plan)

Finnish Proficiency Tuition Waivers, with values updated from the 2027-2028 academic year: Scholarship A worth EUR 2,500 on the basis of a Finnish language proficiency certificate, and Scholarship B worth EUR 1,500 on the basis of studies completed at UEF
100% tuition fee waiver for admitted students who have been granted temporary protection in Finland
Faculties may award discretionary merit-based scholarships to students with outstanding academic achievements
eligibility: Liable to pay tuition fees: citizen of a country outside the EU/EEA area or Switzerland, without an exempting Finnish or EU residence permit
Admitted (offered a study place) to an international Bachelor's or Master's degree programme at UEF for the 2027 intake

For the 30% waiver of later years: at least 55 ECTS credits completed during the first academic year (1 August to 31 July), included in the degree and approved as part of the Personal Study Plan (PSP/HOPS)

For the Finnish Proficiency Tuition Waivers: tuition-fee-paying degree student, Finnish or Swedish was not the language of secondary education, limited or no Finnish skills at enrollment, no previous Finnish Proficiency Tuition Waiver, and improvement or tested skills gained while enrolled at UEF
requirements: Apply through the national Studyinfo application portal during the official application period; a non-waivable application fee applies to applicants from outside the EU/EEA area and Switzerland, except Erasmus Mundus programmes

Accept the offer of admission and pay the tuition fee, or its first instalment, through the Flywire payment system within 21 days of the publication of the admission results to obtain the Early Bird discount
Pay the annual tuition fee by 31 August in later study years, either as a single payment or in two equal instalments

Complete at least 55 ECTS credits during the first academic year, included in the approved Personal Study Plan, and apply during the separate application period organised after the first year of studies

Submit Finnish Proficiency Tuition Waiver applications only during the annual windows: 15 November to 15 December for the spring semester waiver (decision by 15 January) and 15 June to 15 August for the autumn semester waiver (decision by 15 September)
documents: For the Finnish Proficiency Tuition Waiver e-form: name, study right number, degree programme name, e-mail address, and the waiver option chosen (A or B)

Option A evidence: National Certificate of Language Proficiency (YKI) test certificate at intermediate level 3 or 4 (all levels), or the Civil Service Language Proficiency Examination in Finnish (VKT) certificate with satisfactory written and oral skills

Option B evidence: official digitally signed transcript of records from Atomi (available in Peppi) showing the Suomi 3 course or a higher-level course, or 15 ECTS credits of Finnish as a Second Language studies

For verification of a residence-permit-based tuition fee exemption: copies of both sides of a valid residence permit card in Finland and a copy of a valid passport or national ID card indicating citizenship
selection_criteria: Early Bird discount: granted to students liable to pay tuition fees and admitted to the 2027 intake who accept their offer and pay within 21 days of the results; there is no separate application and no limited number of places for it
30% later-year waiver: awarded at the same rate to all students who meet the 55 ECTS and PSP/HOPS criteria; a separate application period is organised after the first year

Finnish Proficiency Tuition Waivers: granted when the published criteria for option A or option B are fulfilled and the application is filed in the correct window; the waiver can be awarded only once during studies and covers one semester
Total waiver cannot exceed 100% of one semester's tuition fee, and any previous partial waiver is capped rather than topped up
coverage: 30% of the first academic year's tuition fee (EUR 3,000-3,600 depending on the programme)
30% of the annual tuition fee in the second and third study years of bachelor's studies and in the second year of master's studies, based on academic progress
Finnish Proficiency Tuition Waivers of EUR 2,500 (Scholarship A) and EUR 1,500 (Scholarship B) from the 2027-2028 academic year, each covering one semester
Living costs, travel and other expenses are not covered: students are expected to have sufficient personal funds for the remaining tuition fees and living expenses throughout their studies
application_method: Apply to the degree programme through the national Studyinfo.fi portal during the application period (7-21 January 2027 for the September 2027 intake, or 1-15 October 2026 for the early Economics and Business Administration window)
Accept the study place and pay the tuition fee or first instalment via Flywire within 21 days of the admission results to secure the Early Bird discount
Pay any second instalment and later annual tuition fees by 31 August
Apply for the 30% progress-based tuition waiver during the separate application period after the first year of studies
Apply for the Finnish Proficiency Tuition Waiver through the UEF e-form during the published annual application windows
official.application_route: Apply to the programme via Studyinfo during the 2027 intake application period; the Early Bird discount requires no separate application and follows automatically from accepting the offer and paying via Flywire within 21 days of the results.
official.citizenship_residency: Tuition fees apply to citizens of countries outside the EU/EEA area and Switzerland. Exemption applies to EU/EEA/Swiss citizens, holders of a Finnish permanent (P) or continuous (A, granted on grounds other than studying) residence permit, P-EU long-term EU resident permits, EU family member residence cards, EU Blue Cards and Brexit SEU/P SEU permits, plus people under temporary protection whose permit is valid at the start of studies. Degree programmes conducted in Finnish remain free of charge regardless of citizenship.
official.international_eligibility: Only students from outside the EU/EEA area and Switzerland can benefit, since they are the applicants liable to pay tuition fees; EU/EEA and Swiss citizens study tuition-free and therefore do not need the waivers.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Available for all international Bachelor's and Master's degree programmes except Erasmus Mundus and Joint Degree programmes, which have their own tuition fee and scholarship arrangements; programme-specific details are published in UEF's programme information table.
official.duration: Early Bird discount covers the first academic year. The 30% tuition waiver covers the second and third study years of bachelor's studies and the second year of master's studies, awarded after the first year. Finnish Proficiency Tuition Waivers are awarded once and cover one semester.
official.description: The University of Eastern Finland offers an Early Bird discount and tuition waivers for tuition fee-paying students, which generally cover up to 30% of the tuition fee. For the first academic year of the 2027 intake, eligible students benefit from a 30% Early Bird discount, and for subsequent years a 30% tuition waiver is awarded based on academic progress, while Finnish Proficiency Tuition Waivers reward achievements in Finnish language studies.
official.program_type: Partial tuition fee waiver: Early Bird discount, progress-based waivers and Finnish Proficiency Tuition Waivers
official.english_requirement: Admission to the English-taught programmes requires demonstrated English proficiency through an approved test (IELTS Academic, TOEFL iBT, PTE Academic, C1 Advanced, C2 Proficiency, or YKI level 5 in the reading, writing and speaking subtests); minimum scores are programme-specific and no waivers are granted. No language test is required when proficiency is shown by a degree completed in English in the listed countries, provided English is clearly stated as the medium of instruction. The tuition waivers themselves carry no separate English requirement.

verification.notes: Amounts, waiver rules, Finnish Proficiency values, payment deadlines and application windows were taken from UEF's own tuition fees page (updated 3 August 2026), the UEF Kamu student handbook (last modified 18 September 2026) and the UEF Master's programmes and language requirements pages. The 500 EUR Early Bird deduction shown on Kamu belongs to the 2026 intake and was not used; the 2027 intake figures are EUR 3,000-3,600 (30%).

applicant_utility.summary: This is a partial tuition discount, not a full scholarship: admitted non-EU/EEA students who accept their offer and pay via Flywire within 21 days of the results automatically save EUR 3,000-3,600, i.e. 30% of the first-year fee. Have the money ready before results are published, because the 21-day payment window is short and missing it forfeits the discount with no route back. Plan to fund the remaining EUR 6,400-8,400 of tuition plus roughly EUR 900-1,000 per month of living costs yourself, since UEF provides no living-cost support and expects proof of funds upfront. If you intend to stay for the whole degree, note that later-year 30% waivers depend on completing at least 55 ECTS in your first year, so pace your studies from day one.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-EU/EEA/Swiss applicants to UEF's English-taught programmes who can pay the bulk of tuition promptly and want a guaranteed discount without competing for a limited quota.
application_readiness_checklist: Line up the full first-year tuition, or at least the first instalment, before admission results are published; the 21-day window is fixed
Prepare Flywire payment access and keep the Studyinfo Learner Number or ID and exact name spelling from the admission letter at hand
Check your programme's actual fee (EUR 10,000 or EUR 12,000) on its programme page, since the discount scales with the fee
Budget the Student Union membership fee and the Kela student healthcare fee on top of tuition
If you hold a qualifying Finnish or EU residence permit, submit scans of both sides of the card plus your passport with the application to request the tuition fee exemption
common_rejection_risks: Paying after the 21-day post-results deadline, which forfeits the Early Bird discount with no obligation for UEF to restore it
Waiting for a first-year scholarship decision: nothing beyond the automatic 30% can be applied for during the application process
Losing the later-year 30% waiver by finishing the first year with fewer than 55 ECTS credits or without them included in the approved PSP/HOPS
Presenting a type A residence permit that was originally granted for study, and being charged full fees despite believing you were exempt
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Remaining 70% of tuition (about EUR 6,400-8,400 in year one), living costs of about EUR 900-1,000 per month, Student Union membership and Kela student healthcare fees, and the non-waivable application fee where applicable
document_audit: Residence permit scans must show both sides and match the passport name used in the application
For the later Finnish Proficiency waiver you need a YKI/VKT certificate or an Atomi-signed transcript; course registrations alone prove nothing
Each Finnish Proficiency waiver applies only to the following semester, so timing the application window matters more than document speed
alerts: UEF reports all waivers and scholarships it awards to the Finnish Tax Administration
If your residence permit is not applied for by 31 July, you cannot defer the waiver and the fee is due in full
Refund requests for first-year fees must be filed by 31 December of the admission year, or the university has no obligation to return the money
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Admission happens first through Studyinfo; the discount is then a payment action, with the offer accepted and the fee paid via Flywire within 21 days of the results.
